For visual poetry, you can’t get much better than *the Color of Pomegranates*. If you want a well explored dynamic between two characters with an emphasis on psychology and isolation, I’d go with *Persona*. *Brand Upon the Brain!* also really scratched the same itch as *the Lighthouse* for me. If all else fails and you just want something absurd and kinda gross to watch, *Singapore Sling*.

Beautiful black and white cinematography, heavy on symbolism, moody and sinister atmosphere, all three classics. And you can't go wrong with Lynch

It reminded me a lot of Bergman's Hour of the Wolf (1968), both in its themes of isolation inside of an island as well as how both films dwell in surreal imagery to showcase the characters' inner turmoils. Though in Bergman's case, those turmoils get a material form that encompasses all the anguish the characters feel, while The Lighthouse is a lot more subtle in that regard.

Also, same old recomendation... just watch the other films by The Lighthouse's director. The Witch has the same melancholic/paranoid ambiance that is great, although I left it feeling a bit more disconcerted than The Lighthouse.

Watch Bergman's Hour of the Wolf (1968), takes place in a similar isolated setting and contains surreal horror elements. Both films have a temporal distortion quality that feeds into the surrealism. Eggers' body of work as a whole owes quite a bit to Bergman.

A movie that really reminded me of The Lighthouse was Woman in the Dunes. Black & white photography, psychologically intense story of two people stuck together in a remote, harsh climate, artsy ambiguity, unsettling atmosphere. In terms of gender dynamics a few moments land a bit weirdly for a modern viewer IMO but otherwise it’s brilliant.
*Climax* does a great job at descending into chaos. It definitely fits under visual poetry as well with the dance numbers and extremely long takes.

'A Pure Formality' starring Polanski as a detective in a run down HQ of provincial France interrogating Gerard Depardieu during a pounding rain storm in an exceptionally atmospheric cat and mouse game. It's a great two-hander like The Lighthouse and the location also plays a formidable role in the work.
